attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The converse is false or at least unproved: absence of small relaxed formula separators does not imply H_N is hard, because an arbitrary H_N circuit may exploit input-level structure that does not factor through a formula predicate.
steps: Define A_N on length-L_N formulas with negative avoidance and positive hitting over generated bags.
Build a circuit for H_N by computing G_N(x), applying A_N to each of the t_N formulas, and ORing the answers.
Therefore a claimed lower bound C(H_N)>N^{1+epsilon-o(1)} forces size(A_N)>N^{1+epsilon-q-o(1)} whenever rho<1+epsilon.
Taking A_N to be a genuine SAT circuit recovers the target bridge: SAT in SIZE(L^c) would imply C(H_N)<=N^{max{rho,q}+o(1)}.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This cycle supplies a valid necessary audit and a sharper falsifier, not a lower bound for H_N. Proving SepHit_N large against unrestricted predicates is already a non-natural-looking pseudorandomness or correlation task.

assumptions: G_N has unrestricted circuit size at most N^{rho+o(1)}.
The top OR and query fanout cost O(t_N L_N) wires/gates under the chosen circuit-size convention.
H_N is measured as a length-N Boolean function in unrestricted nonuniform SIZE.
The separator A_N need not decide SAT on the generated range; it may reject many satisfiable formulas if every positive bag still has one accepted satisfiable formula.
definitions: source object: H_N(x)=OR_{j<=t_N} SAT(phi_{N,j}(x)), where G_N(x)=(phi_{N,1}(x),...,phi_{N,t_N}(x)) outputs t_N=N^q formulas of length L_N=(log N)^d.
target object: SAT on length L_N formulas with nonuniform circuits of size L_N^c, for arbitrary fixed c.
controlled interface: substitute a target SAT circuit or a relaxed formula predicate into each generated query and OR the t_N answers after computing G_N.
target-preserving condition: q<1+epsilon, rho<1+epsilon, no advice depending on x beyond the nonuniform circuits for G_N and the substituted length-L_N predicate.
A relaxed bag separator A_N is a Boolean circuit on length-L_N formulas satisfying negative avoidance and positive hitting over the actual bags generated by G_N.
SepHit_N is the minimum circuit size of such an A_N, with infinity if no separator exists.

equations.label: relaxed_separator_conditions
equations.latex: H_N(x)=0 \Rightarrow \sum_{j\le t_N} A_N(\phi_{N,j}(x))=0,\qquad H_N(x)=1 \Rightarrow \sum_{j\le t_N} A_N(\phi_{N,j}(x))\ge 1.
equations.valid_when: Valid when H_N is exactly the OR of SAT labels on the generated bag and A_N is only required to hit each positive bag once.

equations.label: separator_upper_bound
equations.valid_when: Applies after the generator outputs explicit formulas and the same separator circuit is reused on all t_N query positions.

equations.label: necessary_source_audit
equations.valid_when: Requires the generated-OR source lower bound to be measured against unrestricted nonuniform circuits with subthreshold generator overhead.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Find a length-L_N predicate A_N of size at most N^{1+epsilon-q-delta} that rejects every formula appearing in negative bags and accepts at least one formula in every positive bag.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This is a route-level falsifier lemma: a small SepHit_N certifies that the proposed carrier cannot support the barely-superlinear lower bound needed for magnification.
candidate_lemmas.statement: For the generated-OR carrier, a small relaxed bag separator is a sufficient circuit for H_N. Hence any valid N^{1+epsilon} source lower bound must exclude these separators, not merely range-restricted SAT solvers or selectors.

assumptions: For contradiction, SAT has circuits B_n of size n^c for some fixed c.
t_N=N^q and L_N=(log N)^d, so t_N L_N^c=N^{q+o(1)}.
C(G_N)=N^{rho+o(1)} and max{q,rho}<1+epsilon.
definitions: SAT_L denotes satisfiability restricted to formulas of length L.
A target circuit family B_L for SAT supplies A_N=B_{L_N}.
The length map L_N=(log N)^d is unbounded, so a P/poly family for SAT gives circuits at every queried length L_N.
The implication is route-level and does not by itself prove any lower bound for H_N.

equations.valid_when: Valid when a single length-L_N SAT circuit is substituted into every generated query without extra nonuniform advice leakage.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If the source lower bound is only infinitely often or only for sparse N without a length-coverage certificate, the conclusion weakens to an insufficient length-restricted SAT lower bound.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This preserves the calibrated target consequence while isolating the new source obligation SepHit_N>N^{1+epsilon-q-o(1)}.

assumptions: Positive bags may contain many satisfiable formulas, but the separator may accept only a chosen recognizable subfamily.
Negative bags contain only unsatisfiable formulas by definition of H_N=0.
The generator may leak a marker or statistical artifact correlated with the existence of a satisfying formula.
definitions: U_N is the set of formulas appearing in any generated query position.
A promise SAT solver labels every formula in U_N according to SAT.
A relaxed separator labels only enough formulas to hit all positive bags while avoiding all formulas in negative bags.
A syntactic planted-marker generator can create tiny separators even when promise SAT on U_N remains hard.

equations.label: separator_weaker_than_promise_solver
equations.latex: \operatorname{SepHit}_N\le C(SAT|_{U_N}),\quad\text{and strict separation is possible under planted recognizable positive witnesses}.
equations.valid_when: Valid when the same predicate deciding SAT on U_N satisfies the relaxed separator conditions but the converse labeling requirements are absent.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Construct G_N so every positive bag contains a formula with an easy marker M and no negative bag contains M; then A_N=M collapses H_N below threshold.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This blocks attempts to certify source hardness only through range-restricted SAT hardness; the valid audit must target relaxed bag separators directly.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Lower-bounding SAT on the generated promise range is not enough for this route. A relaxed bag separator can be much smaller than any promise SAT solver because it only needs one accepted witness per positive bag and zero accepted formulas on negative bags.

control_decision.pivot_test: Backtrack if SepHit_N can be bounded below only by natural, dense, efficiently checkable properties or if every explicit generator admits a marker/statistical separator of size below N^{1+epsilon-q}.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote only after proving a non-natural or pseudorandom SepHit_N>N^{1+epsilon-q-o(1)} lower bound for a fully specified generator with q,rho<1+epsilon.
control_decision.reason: The route still has a precise quantitative bridge, but the source obligation is now SepHit_N lower bounds rather than generic carrier hardness.

dependency_updates.description: The SAT-substitution bridge remains valid with size N^{max{rho,q}+o(1)} under q,rho<1+epsilon.
Any source lower-bound attempt must prove SepHit_N>N^{1+epsilon-q-o(1)} for relaxed bag separators.
Range-restricted SAT solver lower bounds are insufficient because relaxed separators need not decide SAT on all generated formulas.

A statistical artifact distinguishing positive witness formulas from negative-bag formulas yields C(H_N)<=N^{q} poly(L_N) despite possible SAT hardness on U_N.
If q>=1+epsilon, even superconstant separator lower bounds cannot preserve the barely-superlinear threshold.
If rho>=1+epsilon, the generator alone violates the valid magnification window.
If the source proof only lower-bounds promise SAT on U_N, it misses relaxed separators and leaves nonuniform leakage open.

L_N=(log N)^d with d>1 so exhaustive truth-table lookup is not a subthreshold explanation.

branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 30 replaces the one-sided selected-image audit by the weaker and more dangerous relaxed bag-separator audit. The valid target bridge is unchanged, but the source lower bound must defeat predicates that merely hit one positive witness per positive bag and avoid all negative-bag formulas. This exposes a concrete nonuniform-leakage falsifier not captured by promise SAT hardness.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Formalize SepHit_N as a bipartite hitting-avoidance problem between positive bags and negative formula occurrences, then test whether random-looking generators satisfy the required lower bound by a counting argument and where explicitness breaks the argument.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The bridge lemma is proved, but applying it to a P-vs-NP route requires an actual separator F_N and a target-preserving polynomial orbit-density certificate. Standard padding can destroy the density certificate while preserving reductions.
steps: Define P_N={X in {0,1}^N:F_N(X)=1}. Constructivity is inherited from the assumed poly(N)-time evaluation of the total separator F_N.
Since F_N(T_N)=1 and F_N is G_N-invariant, every element of the orbit G_N*T_N is in P_N. Therefore density(P_N)>=|G_N*T_N|/2^N.
Usefulness is exactly the assumption F_N(tt(C))=0 for all circuits C of size n^k; no closure of the target class under G_N is needed.
For G_N=S_N, the orbit is the Hamming-weight layer of T_N, so Stirling gives the central threshold | |T_N|_1/N-1/2 | <= O(sqrt(log N/N)) for polynomial density.
For small groups such as AGL(n,2) or S_n acting on input variables, |G_N| is only 2^{polylog N}, so orbit density is exponentially small and invariance alone cannot trigger the natural-proof barrier.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This only classifies a family of lower-bound proof objects as natural or not natural by orbit size. It neither constructs a SAT lower bound nor resolves P != NP.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Barrier-Aware Lower-Bound Route: Orbit Largeness Gate

assumptions: F_N is total on all N-bit truth tables, not merely promised near T_N.
F_N(X)=F_N(gX) for every g in G_N and every X in {0,1}^N.
F_N(T_N)=1 and F_N(tt(C))=0 for every Boolean circuit C of size at most n^k.
The naturalness audit is conditional on standard PRF existence in the target scale; it is route-level barrier control.
definitions: source object: a total group-invariant truth-table separator F_N for a named language slice L_n, with T_N=tt(L_n) and N=2^n.
target object: a Razborov-Rudich natural property useful against SIZE(n^k) truth tables; this is not a proof of P != NP.
controlled interface: an explicit coordinate action G_N<=S_N, poly(N)-time evaluation of F_N, and rejection of every target circuit truth table.
target-preserving condition: the orbit density |G_N*T_N|/2^N is at least N^{-a} and the target circuit exponent k is not weakened.

equations.label: orbit_density
equations.valid_when: Valid when F_N is total, accepts T_N, and is invariant under the explicit group action.

equations.label: natural_density_lower_bound
equations.valid_when: Valid when the source lower-bound model is explicitly named and the target rejection is over all SIZE(n^k) truth tables.

equations.label: full_symmetric_orbit
equations.valid_when: Valid when the group is the full coordinate symmetric group and orbit membership is determined exactly by Hamming weight.

equations.label: entropy_estimate
equations.valid_when: Applies when pN is integral and Stirling errors are controlled uniformly for the stated entropy regime.

equations.label: central_layer_threshold
equations.valid_when: Valid in the central layer regime where epsilon tends to zero and A is fixed independently of N.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: The bridge fails as a naturalization claim if the orbit of T_N has exponentially small density, if F_N is partial or nonconstructive, or if usefulness only rejects an average-case subset of SIZE(n^k).
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Barrier bridge: converts group invariance plus a polynomial orbit-size certificate into a natural-proof object with the same target class.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Let N=2^n and T_N be the truth table of a named source slice L_n. If a total poly(N)-constructive separator F_N:{0,1}^N->{0,1} is invariant under an explicit coordinate group G_N<=S_N, accepts T_N, rejects every SIZE(n^k) truth table, and |G_N*T_N|>=2^N/N^a, then F_N^{-1}(1) is a valid natural property of density at least N^{-a} useful against SIZE(n^k). Thus a large-orbit invariant route is inside the natural-proofs/PRF falsifier scope unless it drops constructivity, largeness, or full usefulness.

assumptions: The only proposed source of largeness is the orbit generated by G_N.
No extra anti-concentration, certificate, or density lemma is supplied.
Target usefulness is still against the same SIZE(n^k) class.
definitions: small group: a coordinate group G_N with log_2|G_N|=o(N).
input affine group: AGL(n,2) acting on N=2^n truth-table positions by affine maps of the n-bit input.
route status: outside this orbit-largeness gate, not automatically outside all natural-proof barriers.

equations.label: max_orbit_density
equations.valid_when: Valid when no stabilizer information stronger than the group-size upper bound is available.

equations.label: affine_group_bound
equations.valid_when: Applies when the symmetry acts on input points by affine transformations over F_2.

equations.label: variable_permutation_bound
equations.valid_when: Applies when the only symmetry is permutation of the n input variables.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If the route supplies an additional polynomial-density accepting region not generated by the small group orbit, this falsifier no longer blocks it.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Falsifier to the slogan that symmetry alone makes a lower-bound certificate natural.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Invariance under a small input-symmetry group is not by itself a natural-proof certificate. If |G_N|=2^{o(N)}, then every orbit has density at most 2^{-N+o(N)}; affine-input, variable-permutation, and low-dimensional syntactic symmetries therefore need an independent density certificate before the natural-proof falsifier applies.

assumptions: r=beta m for a fixed beta>0.
The route relies on full symmetric orbit size as its only largeness source.
Invalid padding strings are rejected and not hidden by advice.
definitions: unique-padding slice: inputs of length M=m+r are accepted only when the last r bits are all zero and the first m bits encode a satisfiable formula.
target transfer: a circuit for SAT_m gives a circuit for L_{m,r} with only padding-check overhead, so lower bounds for L_{m,r} can be target-preserving when M=Theta(m).
orbit mechanism: the group is S_N on the N=2^M coordinates of the padded truth table.

equations.label: padded_density
equations.valid_when: Requires the unique-padding convention where exactly one padding string is legal and all other paddings are rejected.

equations.label: orbit_collapse

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If the encoding is balanced by a target-preserving NP-complete construction with certified central density, this sparse-padding falsifier does not apply.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Encoding audit: separates valid orbit-naturalization thresholds from padding artifacts.
candidate_lemmas.statement: For the unique-padding SAT slice L_{m,r}={x0^r:x in SAT_m}, with r=beta m and beta>0, the full S_N orbit of its truth table is exponentially sparse even if the original SAT slice has constant density. Hence full coordinate symmetry naturalizes only central-density encodings; sparse padding is a concrete falsifier to unconditional symmetry-implies-naturalness claims.

dependency_updates.description: Added an orbit-density criterion: constructive invariant separators with polynomial source orbit become valid natural properties useful against the same target class.
Orbit counting is truth-table black-box. It supplies no nonrelativizing feature unless the separator uses unrelativized syntax in a separately target-preserving way.
The group-orbit argument is combinatorial and does not certify a nonalgebrizing escape. Algebraic encodings still need their own extension-field audit.
Any invariant-separator route must now report |G_N*T_N|/2^N or provide another polynomial-density certificate before invoking natural-proof barriers.

falsifiers: falsifier: the all-zero truth table has orbit density 2^{-N} under every coordinate group, so invariance alone is not largeness.
falsifier: unique-padding SAT with r=beta m has full-symmetric orbit density 2^{-N+o(N)}, invalidating any unconditional symmetry-implies-naturalness claim.
PRF falsifier: a poly(N)-constructive polynomial-density property useful against SIZE(n^k) contradicts sufficiently secure PRFs in that target scale.
Encoding falsifier: balancing SAT by adding a complement copy would generally leave NP unless a separate NP-preserving construction is supplied.
Small-group falsifier: affine-input invariance gives orbit density at most 2^{-N+O((log N)^2)}, far below any valid natural-proof threshold.

branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 30 turns symmetry from a vague barrier label into a quantitative gate. Large coordinate orbits force naturalness; small input-symmetry groups and sparse padded SAT are concrete falsifiers to symmetry-only naturalization. This is valid route-level progress, not evidence for P != NP.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The bridge is conditional on constructing a uniform, low-image-entropy, cap-compatible MCSP source with a real hard accepted image at constant epsilon. No such source is produced here.
steps: Fix an admissible source length m and enumerate accepted certificates lexicographically.
Declare a certificate canonical iff no earlier accepted certificate emits the same truth table; this removes duplicate contamination without requiring a selector for the hard witness.
Build F on q_m=m+ceil(log I_m) bits by interpreting the first block as a canonical image index j and the second block as x in {0,1}^m; output the x-th bit of the j-th canonical table.
If F has a circuit of size s, hardwire the index of a hard accepted image; the resulting m-input circuit computes that hard table with size s+O(q_m).
Thus s>2^{epsilon m-o(m)}, giving exponent epsilon/(1+D) on the multiplex length.
Use the uniform kappa-dense predecessor schedule and padding by ignored variables to transfer the bound to all larger target lengths with loss kappa.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The derivation proves a valid transfer theorem for a named carrier interface. It does not establish the source soundness needed for P != NP, and it remains vulnerable to the cap, advice, and naturalness falsifier tests.

assumptions: For every admissible m, some accepted certificate a has C(V_m(a))>2^{epsilon m} in the ordinary Boolean circuit model.
The number of distinct accepted emitted tables I_m is at most 2^{D m+o(m)} for a fixed finite D.
Duplicate certificates are allowed, but equality of emitted tables is decided by full E-time emission and comparison, not by nonuniform advice.
The admissible source lengths m_i satisfy m_{i+1}<=kappa m_i+O(1), with a uniform predecessor map for padding.
The verifier/emitter itself does not give random access or checkpoint circuits below the claimed MCSP threshold.
definitions: source object: A deterministic E-uniform verifier/emitter V_m with certificates of length at most c m, accepting A_m, and emitting N=2^m bit truth tables for Boolean functions on m inputs.
target object: A single E language F whose length slices are padded multiplexes over the distinct accepted image tables emitted by V_m.
controlled interface: E-uniform canonical unranking of distinct emitted tables, followed by the hardwiring implication from any small multiplex circuit to a small row circuit.

target-preserving condition: The source length set is E-computable and kappa-dense, the image entropy is at most Dm+o(m), certificate enumeration stays in 2^{O(m)} time, no advice selects witnesses or lengths, and epsilon is below the verifier cap alpha_V.

equations.label: image_multiplex_length
equations.valid_when: Valid when distinct emitted truth tables, not accepted certificates, are the multiplex rows and the quotient is E-canonicalized uniformly.

equations.label: row_hardwiring_lower_bound
equations.valid_when: Applies after fixing the multiplex index converts any target circuit into a circuit for the hard accepted row.

equations.label: dense_padding_transfer
equations.latex: \forall \delta<\epsilon/(\kappa(1+D)),\quad C(F_n)>2^{\delta n}\text{ for all sufficiently large }n
equations.valid_when: Requires the kappa-dense source schedule and padding map to be uniform and target-preserving across all intervening lengths.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A falsifier is any source where the quotient/unranking uses advice, I_m exceeds 2^{Dm+o(m)}, the hard witness is outside the accepted image, or padding lengths are chosen nonuniformly.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Main repaired bridge lemma for cycle 30; it computes the exact loss from distinct-image entropy rather than certificate count.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Canonical image-entropy multiplexing bridge: if a uniform MCSP certificate emitter has kappa-dense source lengths, linear certificate scan, distinct accepted-image entropy at most Dm+o(m), and at least one accepted table of circuit complexity greater than 2^{epsilon m} at each source length, then it yields an E language with circuit lower bound exponent every delta<epsilon/(kappa(1+D)). This is a valid route-level transfer, not a proof of P != NP.

assumptions: c and b are constants independent of m.
The emitter outputs the full truth table or a sequential stream in deterministic 2^{O(m)} time.
The target E machine may spend 2^{O(q_m)} time on inputs of length q_m.
definitions: Accepted certificate a is canonical for table T if V_m(a)=T and no lexicographically earlier accepted b emits T.
The j-th multiplex row is the table emitted by the j-th canonical accepted certificate, or the zero table if fewer than j+1 canonical rows exist.
Certificate length c m and emitter time 2^{b m} imply duplicate testing by pairwise full-table comparison in 2^{O((b+c)m)} time.

equations.label: quotient_time
equations.valid_when: Valid when canonicality is tested by comparing each candidate certificate against all earlier certificates using full emitted tables.

equations.label: E_budget
equations.valid_when: Applies only for linear certificates and constant-rate emission; superlinear certificates destroy the E-uniform quotient budget.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If equality of images is supplied by advice, by an oracle, or by superlinear certificate search, the bridge is not valid for the target E lower bound.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Removes a hidden gap from cycle 29: low image entropy is usable without an external quotient oracle.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Duplicate-certificate quotient lemma: for linear certificate length, a canonical enumeration of distinct emitted tables is E-computable even if the accepted certificate set is much larger than the image set.

assumptions: The circuit model is ordinary nonuniform Boolean circuits, with no oracle gates or advice embedded in the carrier.
The verifier profile tau_V(lambda) and configuration exponent sigma are declared before claiming MCSP soundness.
The source proof does not use a constructive dense property that contains most random functions and excludes small circuits.
definitions: alpha_V is the best uniform checkpoint/restart upper-bound exponent forced by the verifier implementation.
A source is non-large if its accepted image density among all 2^m-input truth tables is at most 2^{Dm+o(m)-2^m}.
The bridge is non-natural in the large-property sense because it searches a sparse image, not a dense property of random truth tables.

equations.label: restart_cap
equations.valid_when: Valid when emitted tables can be reconstructed from checkpoint blocks with configuration exponent sigma and block recomputation exponent tau_V(lambda).

equations.label: sparse_density
equations.valid_when: Applies when the accepted image set has entropy Dm+o(m), making the property far from large.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If epsilon>alpha_V, soundness is false; if sparsity is repaired by random salt to become large and constructive, natural-proofs barriers become a substantive falsifier.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Source-side obstruction certificate and barrier audit for proposed carrier families.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Cap-and-naturalness audit: the source construction must be cap-compatible and non-large. Any verifier restart profile that yields circuits of size 2^{alpha_V m+o(m)} for every emitted table refutes source soundness above epsilon>alpha_V; any dense constructive completion revives the natural-proofs falsifier.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot if every plausible low-image source either has alpha_V<epsilon, requires nonuniform quotient advice, or becomes a dense natural property.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if a concrete verifier family supplies E-uniform quotienting, kappa-dense lengths, image entropy D=O(1), epsilon<=alpha_V, and a non-natural proof of one hard accepted image.
control_decision.reason: The bridge lemma is now valid and quantitatively explicit; progress requires constructing or refuting the named source object rather than restating hardness magnification or MCSP folklore.

dependency_updates.description: Canonical multiplexing plus kappa-padding yields E lower-bound exponent delta<epsilon/(kappa(1+D)).
Need E-uniform duplicate-free quotienting and a uniform predecessor map for source lengths; advice-based quotienting is invalid.
Sparse image avoids largeness, but cap violation or salt-based dense completion blocks the route.

falsifiers: Image entropy is secretly measured over certificates rather than distinct emitted truth tables, causing the exponent loss to be understated.
